pr.title: Upgrade an installed multipass with multipass upgrade
pr.head: debacd7e5e8875dc838b6a97ec44c35c8607f6ef

summary: multipass is a password manager with no network code and no dependencies. The layers below this one add install.sh, which installs a tagged release into ~/.local/bin and records what it installed in a receipt, and a release workflow that attests the binary and the installer. This pull request adds multipass upgrade, so someone who installed a release can upgrade it without finding and rerunning the installer by hand.

upgrade does not download or replace the binary itself. It downloads the released install.sh with /usr/bin/curl into a private temporary directory. When gh is installed, it checks the script's attestation against the release's Sigstore bundle. Then it runs the script with /bin/bash, so an upgrade gets exactly the installer's own checks and its atomic rename. upgrade --check only reports whether a newer release is out.

1. It refuses a copy the installer did not install. The receipt must name the running executable, and a checkout install is sent back to its checkout.
  2. It checks the installer before running it. The bundle comes straight from the GitHub release, so the script must match that release's attestation. If a release is published between the two downloads, the check fails instead of passing.
  3. It runs the installer with MULTIPASS_BIN_DIR set to the receipt's directory, plus MULTIPASS_VERSION when you name a version, and passes the installer's exit status through.
The review found one problem: upgrade --check orders a prerelease such as 1.0.0-rc.1 above its own final release, 1.0.0.

cards.title: Terms
cards.html:
• Receipt: the key value file the installer writes under ${XDG_DATA_HOME:-~/.local/share}/multipass-install/, recording the version, the install method, and the installed path.
  • Bundle: multipass.sigstore.json, the release asset that holds the signed build attestation for the binary and install.sh. With it, gh attestation verify needs no login.
  • Release version: three dot-separated numbers with an optional - suffix, such as 0.2.0 or 1.0.0-rc.1.

cards.title: Where this sits
cards.html: This is the top layer of a stack. It sits on the release workflow and install.sh verify (#28), which sits on install.sh (#27). This page shows only this layer's diff. The design is the installer plan, § 2.3.

groups.title: The upgrade module
groups.kicker: How upgrade finds the install, fetches and checks the installer, and runs it
intro: src/upgrade.rs holds all of upgrade's behavior. It takes a Tools value that names the programs to run, the URLs, the receipt, and the running executable. Tools::system fills it with the real paths, and the tests fill it with fake shell scripts in a temporary directory, so no test reaches the network.
The code starts every program by absolute path with a separate argv entry for each argument, so no shell ever parses a URL or a version. A version must pass release_version before it reaches a URL.

files.note: New. The upgrade and check logic, with tests that run it against fake curl, gh, and bash scripts.

checks.text: gh is the first executable found on PATH, skipping relative entries. curl and bash are fixed paths.
These arguments match the installer plan's § 2.3 step 3 exactly. The unit test runs_the_checked_installer_and_passes_its_status_through asserts the full command line.

When the attestation fails, this message says the release workflow did not build the installer. A release published between the two downloads, or a gh too old for these flags, fails here too. The review suggests saying so.
The installer inherits the rest of the environment, so an exported MULTIPASS_VERSION still reaches it when no version is named. The review suggests removing it in that case.

compare breaks a tie on equal numbers by comparing the text, so 1.0.0 sorts below 1.0.0-rc.1. upgrade --check then tells someone running the rc that it is newer than the final release, and exits 0. A prerelease should order below its final release, as SemVer orders them.
With no receipt, and with a receipt naming another file, a debug build in a temporary HOME exited 69 with this message and downloaded nothing.
The receipt is read by the same rule as the installer's receipt_get, the first key value line whose key matches. Paths are compared after canonicalizing both.

groups.title: The command line
groups.kicker: Parsing upgrade, its version, and --check, and keeping them apart from store commands
intro: main.rs gives upgrade its own Parsed variant rather than a Command, because it opens no store and so takes no store path. Parsing refuses any store option with upgrade, a version together with --check, and --check on any other command.

files.note: Adds the upgrade command to parsing, USAGE, and main, with parsing tests.

checks.text: upgrade returns its own exit status: the installer's status, or 1 from --check when a newer release is out.
--store x upgrade and upgrade 0.2 each exit 1 with their messages, run by hand with a debug build.

groups.title: Documentation
groups.kicker: The README's upgrade sentence and the plan's settled details
intro: The README's Install section now says how multipass upgrade works for a release install. The installer plan's § 2.3 records what this pull request settled: the accepted version forms, the options upgrade refuses, and what --check prints for a build newer than the newest release.

files.note: Describes upgrade and --check for a copy installed from a release.
